item.title: Stephen A Smith says what he saw from one team during NFL Week 10 was ‘Super Bowl material’
item.description: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With yet another week of NFL action almost in the books, Stephen A. Smith pointed out the team that impressed him the most. The NFL season is well past the halfway mark, and the true contenders in the league are becoming clearer with each passing week. However, there is one team that stood out the most to Stephen A. Smith after their Week 10 performance, and he believes they have shown him another level. Stephen A. Smith claims Minnesota Vikings’ defence is ‘something to behold’ Speaking on his podcast, Stephen A. Smith praised the Minnesota Vikings for their intense defensive effort against Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. He pointed out how DC Brian Flores has been able to turn the defensive unit into one of the most dangerous in the NFL, and warned the rest of the league that they are true Super Bowl contenders. “I’m here to tell you right now – the Minnesota Vikings are a Super Bowl contender,” Stephen A. Smith said on his podcast. “That defence is something to behold. The loss yesterday was not on Jordan Love. I get it. Minnesota was all over them like white on rice. That defence was absolutely, positively, nightmarish. “Jordan Love faced a career-high 60% pressure rate, taking eight sacks and 12 hits. 11/13 Vikings defenders who had a pass rush generated pressure, with nine defenders having multiple pressures. Jordan Love lost more yards (59) on sacks than the Packers gained rushing the football (56). That is an annihilation. In the two games he has faced Minnesota this year, he has been sacked 12 times and hit 27 times… “This defence, led by Brian Flores, is legit; it’s real. In order to beat the Minnesota Vikings, you gotta be able to run the football. There is no way around it. If you can not run the football against the Minnesota Vikings, you’re toast.” The Vikings’ defence has been lauded all season, but their performance against the Packers this weekend showed that they have unlocked a new level. And after solving their QB woes by trading for Kirk Cousins, the Vikings are a team with very few standout weaknesses, and could be Super Bowl-bound. Read more: What Stephen A. item.title: 76ers’ Jaylen Brown left bloodied after scary collision with Julius Randle
item.description: Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images 76ers’ Jaylen Brown left bloodied after scary collision with Julius Randle appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Monday, the P hiladelphia 76ers were trying to hold off the Brooklyn Nets in the fourth quarter after the Nets cut into what was once a 24-point lead for Philly. But with around nine minutes remaining in the fourth, the 76ers encountered some trouble when Jaylen Brown collided headfirst with Julius Randle’s chin — with Brown bearing the brunt of that impact. Brown received the ball on the high post area, spinning away from his defender, Nets guard Keon Ellis. Sensing danger, Randle rotated over. However, the 76ers star careened straight onto Randle, and both of them fell immediately. Brown immediately clutched onto his head after being left bloodied by the blow he took. Jaylen Brown just took a tough shot to the head bumping into Julius Randle here. He's bleeding from the forehead, but got up and walked to the bench on his own power for treatment. pic.twitter.com/Rkwxh6SnE8 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Erin Grugan (@eringrugan) November 17, 2026 Brown is band in the back on the bench applying pressure to his head. He gives a thumbs up here https://t.co/DeBOq06yoQ pic.twitter.com/HB2fH7rnmM — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) November 17, 2026 Both Brown and Randle exited the game after that collision, with Tyrese Maxey and Michael Porter Jr. coming in, respectively, to relieve those two players. The good news for the 76ers was that Brown only needed to miss three minutes of game time. He returned to action with 6:02 left in the fourth, and he helped Philly keep the Nets at bay. Perhaps as a matter of precaution, the 76ers pulled Brown with 1:44 still remaining in the game. They were up by just seven at that point, and the Nets even cut the 76ers’ lead to just four on the subsequent possession, but Philly was confident enough in the talent they had out on the court that they could afford to give Brown a few extra minutes of rest. Brown was phenomenal for the 76ers on Monday. He tallied 31 points, 13 rebounds, and four assists on 9-of-19 shooting from the field, and supporting Joel Embiid in his stellar 37-point outing in what ended up being a 135-123 victory over the Nets. The 76ers have a day off tomorrow before heading to Orlando to face a Magic team that’s currently on a four-game winning streak, and it remains to be seen if Brown would be given the night off for that game. item.title: Former Champion Jorge Linares Arrested By ICE Agents Monday
item.description: What to Know Four-time world champion Jorge Linares announced via social media early on Monday, November 15, that he had been arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents at the El Paso border crossing with Mexico. The nature of the arrest is not known. A nationally known immigration law firm now represents Linares. The four-time world champion retired in 2023 and was added to the International Hall of Fame ballot this year. Fans and followers of four-time former world champion Jorge “El Nino de Oro” Linares were shocked to see a post on his X/Twitter account early on Monday morning. It was brief. Me tiene el ICE en el paso Texas. Que locura — Jorge Linares (@JorgeLinares) November 15, 2026 Linares reported he had been taken into custody by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at the United States / Mexican border in El Paso, Texas shortly after 8 a.m. ET/5 a.m. PT. Four-Time World Champion Jorge Linares is a four time world champion, and now on the International Boxing Hall of Fame ballot. Linares, 41, a native of Venezuela, currently resides in Miami, Florida. Widely regarded as among the most skilled and exciting boxers of his generation in the smaller weight divisions, Linares won world titles in three weight divisions in 21 years at featherweight, super featherweight, and lightweight. Linares won his first world title in 2007. He later added the WBA World Super Featherweight title in 2008, and the WBA and WBC World Lightweight titles from 2014 to 2018. Linares retired in 2023 after a loss to Jack Catterall of England in Liverpool. He retired with a record of 47-9, 29 KOs. For much of his career, Linares lived and trained in Japan. Photo: RicardoCelis/X In a second update, the law firm representing Linares, immigration law specialists Wilner and O’Reilly , posted a letter confirming its role in the case. “Wilner and O’Reilly confirms that it represents Jorge “El Nino de Oro” Linares, the Venezuelan boxer and world champion, following his recent detention by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). “Mr. Linares is legally present in the United States and has fully cooperated with the authorities. Linares posted photos and a message to his hundreds of thousands of followers. “What an incredible honor to be invited to the International Boxing Hall of Fame weekend. “Standing among the legends of boxing reminded me how blessed I have been throughout my career. I want to thank the International Boxing Hall of Fame for their hospitality, and thank all of my fans who have supported me through every victory and every challenge. “God willing, I hope to return next year, and with the support of my fans and the grace of God, I hope that one day my name will also be inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame. “Thank you for the memories, the respect, and the love. This was truly special.” Here’s hoping “El Nino de Oro” is able to join the celebration, whether as a member of the Class of 2027 or an honored guest.

item.title: Watch Rangers raise banner to celebrate 100th anniversary of first-ever game
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Watch Rangers raise banner to celebrate 100th anniversary of first-ever game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Rangers marked a major milestone on Monday night, raising a banner to the rafters at Madison Square Garden to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the franchise’s first-ever game . Exactly 100 years to the day after their NHL debut, the Rangers held a special ceremony at their game against the Montreal Canadiens. The players looked on from the ice as the commemorative banner made its way up to the Garden rafters. The night served as the Rangers’ “Centennial Capstone Game,” closing out a season-long celebration of the franchise’s history. It also kicked off the NHL’s Original Six Series , featuring three all-Original Six matchups in three days. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Blueshirts’ history began on Nov. 16, 1926, when they hosted the Montreal Maroons, the defending Stanley Cup champions. The Rangers announced their arrival in style, blanking the Maroons 1-0 in front of an estimated crowd of 13,000. Bill Cook scored the franchise’s first goal at 18:37 of the second period, and it held up as the winner. Goaltender Hal Winkler was the star of the night, turning away all 48 shots he faced to secure the shutout. That game was played at the third version of Madison Square Garden, located about a mile north of the team’s current home. The Rangers went on to win the Stanley Cup in just their second season, in 1928. A century later, the Rangers are once again facing a team from Montreal. The Canadiens came into the night with a 12-4-4 record, while New York entered at 12-8-1. Adam Fox has led the way for the Rangers this season with a team-high 23 points, including 21 assists. Interestingly, the Canadiens were without former Rangers forward Chris Kreider , who is sidelined for six to eight weeks with an injury. The Rangers will look to cap off their historic night at the Garden with a fitting win over their Original Six rivals. item.title: Red Sox Making Very Smart Decision With Willson Contreras After Jake Bauers Deal
item.description: Red Sox Making Very Smart Decision With Willson Contreras After Jake Bauers Deal originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . When it was announced that the Boston Red Sox planned to sign Jake Bauers to a four-year deal, questions immediately arose about whether Willson Contreras would be moved or lose some of his at-bats. However, given that he was among the best hitters in the Red Sox's lineup a year ago, if not the best, it wouldn't have made much sense for Boston to go either way. That's why the latest report, which should have Red Sox fans very happy, should clear things up about what the organization plans to do. This wasn't to replace Contreras, but more so just to add another really good bat to the lineup on top of what Contreras can do. “That list brings up a good question: What happens to Contreras now? He led the team in home runs (27) and RBIs (81) last year, and was second (4.0) behind Ceddanne Rafaela (4.1) in fWAR. Actually, that’s an easy answer: He and Bauers are likely to split time between first base and DH,” Ken Rosenthal wrote . As long as both guys are in the lineup, there shouldn't be too much of an issue here for the Red Sox. item.title: ‘Josh Allen is NOT a top 3 MVP candidate’: Ryan Clark takes a stand
item.description: Jan 11, 2026; Jacksonville, FL, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) warms up before an AFC Wild Card Round game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images The Buffalo Bills are rolling, improving to 8-1 on the season with a 31-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday. And as usual, quarterback Josh Allen is right in the middle of the MVP conversation. But former NFL safety Ryan Clark isn’t buying it. On Monday, Clark made it clear that he doesn’t think Allen belongs among the top three MVP candidates, and he took particular issue with how Allen’s touchdown totals are being used to build his case. Allen’s MVP Case Allen, who won MVP in 2024, has been his usual productive self in 2026. Through nine games, he has thrown for 2,223 yards with 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions, while adding 11 rushing touchdowns. The rushing touchdowns have been a big part of his MVP case, with Allen racking up 24 total touchdowns so far. And the Bills own the best record in the AFC after winning their fifth straight game on Sunday. But some other quarterbacks have put together big seasons, too. Joe Burrow, who has drawn plenty of praise this season, threw for 409 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals’ 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night, as the Bengals improved to 7-2. Brock Purdy threw for 389 yards in the San Francisco 49ers’ 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys, and the 49ers are now 8-1. Trevor Lawrence also had a big afternoon, throwing for 352 yards in the Jacksonville Jaguars’ 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans to improve to 7-2. ‘Not a Top 3 MVP Candidate’ With all that elite play from the quarterback position this year, Clark made his MVP picks on Monday, and Allen didn’t make the cut. “Josh Allen is NOT a top 3 MVP candidate! Joe Burrow. Brock Purdy. Trevor Lawrence. That’s my 3! Love Josh, but we can’t confuse who he IS with how he’s PLAYING!” Clark wrote on X . Clark also took a shot at the way Allen’s rushing touchdowns have been used to boost his MVP case. “And enough with the total TD graphics! We KNOW he has 8 QB sneak TDs. They count, and they take toughness & skill, but they aren’t equivalent to what Joe, Brock & Trevor are doing! All TDs count. They don’t all tell the same MVP story!” Clark wrote. Clark has never been one to shy away from strong takes, and this one drew plenty of pushback from Bills fans in the replies. Even so, his point about Allen’s passing numbers is hard to ignore, as Allen’s 2,223 passing yards rank just 14th in the NFL. Needless to say, Bills fans probably won’t be changing their minds anytime soon. item.title: Jets reportedly received ‘bad’ intel on Liam Coen before hiring Aaron Glenn
item.description: Photo by Adam Hunger/Getty Images The New York Jets reportedly received misleading information about Liam Coen during their search for a head coach, which helped steer the franchise towards hiring Aaron Glenn instead. The revelation has raised fresh questions about the decision-making behind Glenn’s appointment. According to the New York Post’s Brian Costello, the Jets carried out their research on Coen but were given a negative assessment of his suitability for the role. That decision looks particularly costly now, with Coen enjoying an impressive start to life as Jacksonville Jaguars head coach while Glenn continues to struggle in New York. Mike Tannenbaum reportedly among those who advised against Liam Coen Speaking on Gang’s All Here , Costello explained how the Jets were reportedly discouraged from pursuing Coen. “What happened with Liam Coen with the Jets is I was told they got bad information,” Costello said. He added: “They were told that he wasn’t a good fit; they were told he might not be a good head coach. They were like–they did their due diligence on Liam Coen like they did on everybody. And the scouting report, so to speak, that they got a Liam Coen has turned out to be completely incorrect. They were talking to the wrong people.” Costello indicated that the group providing the information included former Jets general manager Mike Tannenbaum, who now works as an analyst for ESPN. Coen has since guided Jacksonville to a 7-2 record and the top spot in the AFC South. The Jaguars are also the third seed in the AFC, with Coen having made an impressive start to his head coaching career. Glenn, meanwhile, has a 5-22 record since taking charge of the Jets. New York sit just one win above the bottom-placed Miami Dolphins. The situation has also brought renewed scrutiny of Glenn’s leadership. After spending four seasons as Detroit Lions defensive coordinator, he was expected to take a more CEO-like approach in New York, but his coaching appointments have also come under criticism. The Jets have a decision to make about Glenn’s future, with general manager Darren Mougey and owner Woody Johnson ultimately responsible for determining whether he remains in charge beyond this season. item.title: Los Angeles Rams Announce Bad News for Matthew Stafford
item.description: Matthew Stafford and the Rams got more bad news on the injury front. Getty The hits keep coming for Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams, with the latest being the loss of starting center and Super Bowl champion Coleman Shelton. “Rams center Coleman Shelton suffered a hamstring strain and is expected to miss 4-6 weeks, per team spokesperson,” the LA Daily News’ Adam Grosbard reported in a post on X on November 16. Others soon corroborated the report. Rams center Coleman Shelton suffered a hamstring strain against Cardinals and will be out 4 to 6 weeks, a team official said. — Gary Klein (@LATimesklein) November 17, 2026 This news comes after the Rams placed Shelton’s replacement, Dylan McMahon on injured reserve. McMahon must miss at least four games. Rams Lose Super Bowl Champion Coleman Shelton to Hamstring Injury The Rams are on their bye in Week 11. That means that McMahon will now be sidelined at least until Week 16. Moreover, Shelton will be out anywhere from Week 15 through Week 17 after suffering his injury in Week 10 against the Arizona Cardinals. LA was also without starting right guard Steve Avila and backup Justin Dedich. As it stands, their remaining interior options are Beau Limmer, Bill Murray, and David Quessenberry, who is a tackle. Limmer was the Rams’ starting center during the 2024 season. This is the latest setback on the injury front. LA is without starting wide receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua, tight end Terrance Ferguson, defensive back Jaylen Watson, and defensive linemen Kobie Turner and Poona Ford (who is out for the season). Shelton, 31, was an undrafted free agent. He was a member of the 2021 Super Bowl team. He spent one year with the Chicago Bears after signing as a free agent in 2024. Shelton returned to LA in the same fashion in 2025. He has started 59 of his 100 games with the Rams. Stafford has called Shelton a “vital” part of what the team wants to do as an offense. The QB cited the center’s communication even in hostile environments during games. That is what the Rams will miss the most. “He’s vital. He’s vital. His ability to communicate, in loud environments, what we want to get done quickly, concisely, and clearly for all those guys up front was integral in how well we played both in the run game and the pass game,” Stafford told reporters in August. “Setting the fronts quickly. ‘Here we go. Let’s push the tempo’ and the only way you can do that is if everybody’s aligned up front. “He does such a great job of communicating and spreading that word down the line of scrimmage for those guys, so they can play with a quiet mind and play fast and physical.” The Rams have two road games over the projected timeline for Shelton’s return. However, they are against the Rams’ top competition in the NFC West, the division-leading San Francisco 49ers and the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. The Baltimore Ravens made unwanted history in the first half of their showdown against the winless Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore. item.title: Lakers’ Austin Reaves Remains Out as Walker Kessler Joins Injury List vs. Hornets
item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The Los Angeles Lakers ruled out Walker Kessler and Austin Reaves for Tuesday, Nov. 17th clash against the Charlotte Hornets. Austin Reaves’ injury outlook Reaves missed Sunday’s game against the Phoenix Suns after suffering a heel injury last week against the Milwaukee Bucks. Even after three full days of rest, Reaves was not ready to play against the Suns, and now, almost a week later, he is still out. The X-rays on his heel came back clean, meaning there is no structural damage to his foot, and it is labeled as a bruise. Overall, when speaking to the media, head coach JJ Redick does not seem too concerned. “He’s improving,” Redick said. “It really comes down to just like a pain tolerance thing. Again, nothing structural beyond a bruise. And so I think every day it’s been better, and we’ll see where he’s at in 48 hours when we play on Tuesday. The Lakers have a back-to-back coming up, with the Hornets game followed by another home game against the Utah Jazz. Perhaps LA is holding him out until Wednesday’s game, though they may wait until Friday, Nov. 20th against the Sacramento Kings. The Jazz, Hornets, and Kings are among the worst teams in the league, and the Lakers may rest Reaves for much of this stretch. Why Kessler will be sorely missed Meanwhile, on the big-man front, Walker Kessler is out on Tuesday for the first time this year. He appeared on the injury report with right lower leg soreness. Without Kessler, things will get quite hairy for the Lakers on the big-man front. Kevon Looney, the veteran center, may get the start, though he has struggled this year and has been a defensive liability due to his lack of mobility. Overall, Looney is a plodding big man who offers nowhere near the rim protection and movement that Kessler does as both a lob threat and shot-alterer. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The other option will be Carson Cooper, who is on a two-way contract. If the Lakers want to play some small-ball and move away from their size options, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Jared Vanderbilt can play center. Their lack of size costs the team on the boards, but they are strong enough to hold their own against other centers in limited stretches. No matter which path they start with, it will end up looking like a mix of both approaches. item.title: Patriots' AJ Brown Trade Considered 'Laughable' as Injuries and Struggles Continue
item.description: Patriots' AJ Brown Trade Considered 'Laughable' as Injuries and Struggles Continue originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It's almost tough to justify the New England Patriots making that trade for A.J. Brown now. The hope was that Brown would be among the best wide receivers in the NFL, similar to what he's been throughout much of his career. Unfortunately, after the Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder for the disgruntled star with the Philadelphia Eagles at the time, nothing has gone as planned. Whether it's because Brown has been dealing with injuries or because he isn't the same wide receiver he once was, it's obvious this trade hasn't been a positive one for New England. This season, Brown has just 11 receptions for 428 yards. There hasn't been a game yet where he looks even decent, or like the shell of himself he was in Philadelphia. As for how some fans and writers feel about the situation in New England, the frustration is at an all-time high. When recently examining the situation, one writer went as far as to say that the inability to do anything positive this year has almost been funny. “The A.J. Brown trade keeps looking worse by the day. A.J. Brown’s inability to do anything positive this year has been almost laughable. He got hurt in the first game, missed a good chunk of time on injured reserve, came back, was a non-factor, and then got hurt again. He returned on Sunday, was unable to get open and had a drop as well. “He finally made a nice catch-and-run to move the stick on a third down, and then promptly went to the locker room with a hamstring injury. It’s been a rough year for Brown, and the Patriots front office: they effectively bid against themselves to trade for him and still gave up a first-round pick in 2028 to do so. Unless he somehow manages a complete 180, the trade is going to go down as a massive failure, and potentially hamstring the Patriots for years to come,” Pat Lane wrote . It really doesn't make much sense that Brown is playing at this level, unless that injury is as bad as it could be. The reality is that if he’s still dealing with that injury, we're not going to see the same type of player we're used to seeing. However, Brown just hasn't been able to do anything on the offensive side of the football and looks like he’s lost a ton of burst. I'm not ready to say this is one of the worst trades the Patriots have made in a long time, but if it doesn't change soon, it'll be tough to say otherwise. The Ravens QB suffered an awkward fall as one of his linemen was pushed into him as he was throwing. Luckily, he shook that off and avoided any significant injury. Then, he had his first interception as a Raven after quite a wacky play in the second quarter. As Brissett was targeting Ja’Kobi Lane, Chargers cornerback Cam Hart was able to deflect the ball right onto the waiting arms of linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips for the pick . Omarion Hampton converted a fourth-down on the goal-line for his fourth touchdown of the season. Brissett the Ravens would pull three points back with a field goal right at the end of the first half to cut the lead to 17-10. Aside from his injury scare and wacky pick, Brissett was busy in the first half. He threw the ball 23 times, with 14 completions for 163 yards. item.title: Oregon's Dan Lanning talks Evan Stewart, short week ahead of MSU game
item.description: Oregon football coach Dan Lanning predictably wouldn't go into the specifics of his verbal spat with fifth-year receiver Evan Stewart just before halftime of the Ducks ' win vs. Michigan Nov. 14, but he did offer clarity on the receiver's status vs. Michigan State after Stewart didn't play in the second half. Stewart appeared visibly upset after quarterback Dylan Raiola threw a pass out of bounds on third down with 1:49 left to play in the first half and got into a heated argument with Lanning heading into the locker room. The receiver only played 22 snaps the entire game, compared to 58 for Dakorien Moore and 55 for Jeremiah McClellan, the other starting receivers. "I’ll just say that football in a lot of ways is like a family," Lanning said Nov. 16. "You’ll have disagreements at times. He’s a passionate player, I’m a passionate coach. We’ll keep that within us, but I know how much he wants to do a good job for this team and for himself personally and I have expectations that he can create that moving forward." Stewart missed time earlier this season following his DUII arrest , but has been reliable when he's been on the field, catching 36 passes for 508 yards and four touchdowns in eight games. Lanning said Stewart would be available this week against Michigan State. Lanning also mentioned starting offensive guard Douglas Utu practiced Monday and "is going to be in good shape" following a fourth quarter injury vs. Michigan and running back Jordon Davison, who has missed each of the past two games for Oregon, is out of his boot. Lanning talks short week ahead of travel to Michigan State Though the Spartans have struggled this season, Lanning is expecting a stiff test against former longtime Northwestern coach Pat Fitzgerald's squad, in his first year in East Lansing. He cited toughness and a certain level of physicality that previous Fitzgerald teams have played with that the Ducks will need to match if they want to avoid getting upset Friday night on the road. That, and adapting to a long travel day out to Michigan on a short week. "I think our players understand, like OK, you’re going to get a lot shoved in early in the week and you’ll have to absorb it and be able to play into what do we do well already and how can we build off that?" Lanning said. "What can we carry over that we feel like our players can execute at a high level?" The Ducks and Spartans will meet Nov. 20 in East Lansing at 5 p.m. PT. item.title: Darius Garland Believes Clippers Are Moving in Right Direction After Win vs Hornets
item.description: Following a woeful start to the season, the Los Angeles Clippers look like they are figuring some things out. The Clippers (4-8) lost seven straight games after beating the Sacramento Kings in their season opener. However, they have since steadied the ship and won three of their last four — including two in a row. Los Angeles backed up its huge home win against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Friday with another against the Charlotte Hornets at Intuit Dome on Sunday. The Clippers triumphed 113-105 behind 27 points, six rebounds, and seven assists from star point guard Darius Garland. Momentum Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images It doesn't take a lot for elite athletes to find some confidence and start building momentum. The Clippers are proving that right now. Garland acknowledged that the OKC win was massive for the team, whether the former champions are shorthanded or not. "Coming into [the Hornets] game, finishing it pretty well, that was another step [towards] some good success," he said . "We're starting to figure out what we want to do on the offensive and defensive end. We're [getting] comfortable with that." Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Although Garland is still being pestered by turnover issues (4.9 per game), he did enough all over the floor to set the tone for the Clippers against Charlotte. Garland, who leads L.A. in scoring with 21.3 points, shot 10-for-18 from the field (3-for-7 3PT) and was a team high +12 despite committing six giveaways. The Clippers were extremely efficient as a collective, shooting 55 percent from the field and 52 percent from beyond the arc. They nailed 16 triples while holding the Hornets to just 38 percent shooting (33% 3PT). Charlotte made one more three-pointer than the Clippers on 21 more attempts. Better In The Clutch Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The biggest sign of the Clippers' improvement was their execution down the stretch. The hosts locked up the win behind a 29-22 fourth-quarter run, finally pulling away after a back-and-forth contest. The Clippers racked up 32 assists on 41 made field goals. They played team basketball , with everybody chipping in. Four bench players scored in double figures en route to 55 second unit points. Derrick Jones Jr. was the only other starter with 10+ points. He dropped 13 on 5-for-5 shooting (3-for-3 3PT). Off the pine, Max Strus led the way with 14 points on 5-for-8 shooting (4-for-5 3PT). Isaiah Jackson added 13 points (4-for-5 FG), three blocks, and one steal. Gradey Dick (12) and Keaton Wagler (12) combined for 24 points. Dick went 2-for-2 from deep while Wagler notched four rebounds and five assists. The Clippers led by as much as 17 points. They will look to continue their ascent against the Utah Jazz (1-13) on Tuesday.

Mitchell Santner ruled out of Test series with an injury. New Zealand Test squad for India Test series 2026 New Zealand named a 14-man squad for the two-Test series against India, and three of the players on the list are still working their way back from injuries. Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra and Tom Blundell have all been picked even though none of them had fully recovered. The selectors appear to have decided that these three are too important to leave out, and they will be hoping each player is match-ready by the time the first Test arrives. Conway picked up a concussion during a training session just before the ongoing ODI series began. Ravindra has been dealing with a shoulder problem since September, when he was hurt during a commercial photoshoot. Blundell, for his part, is recovering from a quadriceps issue. Head coach Rob Walter has already turned his attention to a busy home season, and he is pleased that a big-name side like India will be the visitors. The squad is largely consistent with the team that competed in England earlier this year, so it’ll be great to be back together to try and recreate some of that success on home soil,” he said. The coach was equally happy with the turnout at the white-ball games so far, and he hopes the same energy will be there when the longer format begins. Fans have shown up in good numbers during the limited-overs matches, which has lifted the mood in the dressing room. “We’ve experienced great crowds so far during the white-ball series, and we’re really looking forward to having that support during the Tests,” Walter added. New Zealand currently sit on top of the World Test Championship standings, and a few more wins against India would only make their position stronger. item.description: While the head coach, players and Spanish press were magnanimous in defeat, there was pride mixed in with disappointment – and confidence the future is still bright “With every game, defeat gets closer,” Luis de la Fuente had said and on Sunday night it finally came. Spain had lost only one competitive game since Scotland in March 2023 back when the coach hadn’t won anything and didn’t look like he ever would – and that solitary loss was on penalties in the 2025 Nations League final . Statistically, they said, penalties don’t count, so while Portugal lifted the trophy that night, the team that won the European Championship and World Cup in the summers either side also claimed a Fifa record of 44 official games unbeaten. And then England turned up at the Metropolitano . A night that started with Iker Casillas, Fernando Torres and Fernando Llorente handing the World Cup to Unai Simón ended with Spain trying to overhaul a shock 3-0 deficit. Against 10 men and led by a superb Lamine Yamal, Spain made De la Fuente think for a while that they would too, but it wasn’t to be. Continue reading...

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.title: Three Lions’ win over Spain comes in two acts: the first superb, the second heroic | Sid Lowe
item.description: Visitors take game to world champions and, though their hold on possession plummets, their rearguard is outstanding In the final, absurdly tense moments before England finally did it and Spain finally fell, when Dan Burn had been sent on to do Dan Burn things, when the board had gone up with a 4 on but the clock wasn’t moving fast enough and the men in red kept coming back, Harry Kane had come to the side of the pitch to stand beside Thomas Tuchel. Palms out, Kane signalled and directed and appealed with his teammates to hold on to what they had: s omehow, anyhow . What they had was special, but their grip on it was not as secure as it had seemed. Not as secure as it should have been too. Tuchel gave Kane a nudge that looked pretty playful considering the pressure, before Marc Bollengier, the fourth official, ordered him back to the bench. But England’s captain was not gone for long and when he returned he was joined by almost all of them, awaiting the big moment. From there, he watched James Trafford make an astonishing double save, a moment of heroism that allowed them to hang on. Then, standing alongside the rest who could no longer just sit there, he saw the last header clear – Dan Burn things – before the whistle went. Then he and they went on one last run, back on to the pitch. Continue reading...

item.title: Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?
item.description: The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years There are days football fans hope will never come. For 23 years, Cristiano Ronaldo has been more than the country’s greatest footballer; he has been its defining sporting figure, a symbol of national pride and constant presence in the lives of supporters. After 234 appearances and 146 goals, the No 7 brought that chapter to a close and on Saturday night the team will play their first game without him . The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
